llm-event-time.history_reference: New mechanism: the direction of single fact records of the reader agents, placed at the publication time of the news document, against the market-relative return of the asset's perpetual contract from minutes after the publication. Family llm-multiagent-v2 (six attempts, all FAIL, closed 2026-11-17) tested the same agents and partly the same records at decisions once a week or once a day, about ten hours or more after the news, as a ranking of the cross-section; it is a different mechanism and is cited as history. Its records are reused here. The earlier no-go on event-driven news trading (2026-07-14) rested on published studies, not on a test in this repository.

reader-records-minute-bars-2023-2024.history_reference: Fact records of the reader agents over news documents (page archive of three outlets, extracted under Charter 2; news feed archive of 67 further outlets, extracted under Charter 5), placed at the publication time of the document, joined with minute bars of the perpetual contracts of the same assets. The daily and weekly returns of the window are exposed: features built from these records were joined with weekly returns (Charters 2 and 5), weekly realised variance (Charter 3) and next-day returns (Charter 4), all FAIL. The minute bars of the window were used by an earlier program on passive execution (exec-pf, 2026-09), without any text. Before this registration no record was joined with a price at or around its publication time; the event table, the lead rule and the counts were built from text stores only, and the noise pass rate and the power of the gate were measured on the events moved back by 104 weeks with random signs.

llm-event-time-run-20261120.question: Does the direction that the reader agents give to an asset-specific news event (favourable or unfavourable) separate the market-relative return of the asset's perpetual contract from 5 minutes after the publication to 4 hours later, on the lead events of 2023 and 2024? Gate: slope of the return on the sign with one intercept per year, standard error clustered by day, t at least 2.0 with a positive slope, and a positive slope in both years. The descriptive tables show how much of the move happens before the publication and in the first minutes.
